lead: The umbilical cord lies below the presenting part. A true emergency: cord compression and vasospasm can kill the fetus within minutes. About 1 in 300–500 deliveries.
f: Cord presentation: membranes intact, cord felt through them · Cord prolapse (overt): membranes ruptured, cord in the vagina or at the vulva · Occult prolapse: cord beside the presenting part, not felt; suspect from FHR dips

sc: Intact membranes, cord felt below the head on VE → Cord presentation

f: Anything that leaves the presenting part not fitting the pelvis · Malpresentation: footling breech (about 15%), complete 5%, frank 0.5%; transverse, oblique, unstable lie · Preterm, low birth weight, PPROM · Second twin · Polyhydramnios: gush at ROM · Multiparity, high head (CPD, praevia) · ARM with a high head, ECV, internal version, balloon induction
Compression between the presenting part and the pelvis · Vasospasm of the umbilical arteries from cold, drying and handling · Result: acute fetal hypoxia; death or brain injury within minutes

Labour going well, membranes rupture (or ARM), then sudden fetal bradycardia or variable decelerations · Mother well, no bleeding, clear liquor · VE at once after any ROM followed by an abnormal FHR · Pulsating cord = fetus alive · Still cord: check the heart by Doppler or bedside scan (may be spasm) · Diagnosis is clinical: no other test

sc: ARM at 5 cm, FHR falls to 80, loop of cord in the vagina → Cord prolapse: call help, push the head up
Mother well, fresh bleed after ROM, FHR 70 → Vasa praevia

f: Call help, note the time; stop oxytocin · Hands off the cord: do not push it back; if outside, tuck it gently into the vagina · Elevate the presenting part with two fingers and keep it up until delivery · Long transfer: fill the bladder with 500 mL warm saline, clamp; empty it before the uterine incision · Position: knee-chest, or exaggerated left Sims for transfer · Terbutaline 0.25 mg SC stops contractions

tr: Never try to replace the cord in the uterus
In a moving ambulance use exaggerated left Sims, not knee-chest

f: Alive, 1st stage: Category 1 CS, decision to delivery ≤ 30 min (GA, or spinal if quick) · Alive, fully dilated, head low: forceps or ventouse in the room · Fully dilated, head high or transverse lie: caesarean · Second twin: breech extraction or ventouse · Dead fetus: vaginal, no CS for the baby · Before 24 wk (limit of viability): counsel; managed as a miscarriage (RCOG; local units: 26 wk)

sc: Pulsating cord prolapse at 4 cm → Category 1 caesarean
Pulsating cord, fully dilated, head +2 → Forceps or ventouse
Cord prolapse, no fetal heart on scan → Vaginal delivery

f: Neonatal team at delivery: asphyxia, HIE · Cord blood gases · Active 3rd stage: PPH risk after tocolysis, CS or instruments · Document times: prolapse, decision, delivery; debrief the mother
Do not do ARM; abandon an ARM if the cord is felt · Preterm: conservative · Term: counsel; most end in caesarean · In labour: caesarean

No ARM with a high head · Needed ARM (polyhydramnios, unstable lie): controlled ARM in theatre, head held at the brim · Admit unstable lie from 37 wk · Check for cord after ECV or internal version · VE and FHR after every ROM in a woman at risk
